newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle markets quiet Friday - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle markets quiet Friday - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with most of the week's showlists sold following active midweek sales at $72.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
Several loads of the cattle sold were picked up within two to three days, which suggested that several packers were short bought on live cattle supplies, the sources said.
A few loads of lower quality cattle sold at $71.00 Friday, amounting to about 200 to 400 head, they said.
Cattle early next week were expected to be priced at $73.00, with bids at $72.00, the feedlot sources said.

Showlists next week were expected unchanged to slightly higher than this week's, which were estimated at 57,000 head for the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and 62,000 for Kansas, market sources said.

Feedlot cattle prices were buoyed by tight supplies of choice cattle, higher boxed beef prices this week and firm retail demand for features the next two weeks going into Thanksgiving and the week following the holiday.
Slaughter Monday will be reduced because of the Veterans Day holiday. IBP said its plants at Amarillo, Texas, Emporia, Kan., and West Point, Neb. would be closed.
National Beef Packing said its Liberal, Kansas, plant also would be closed.
